_law: id_detection_order and prompt_detection_order are SEPARATELY encoded (sdlab v2 product law — never flatten into one list). id-order follows the canon listing convention (ferro pole, chrome pole, the between, then the composites). prompt-order is tuned so the most-specific register keywords resolve first: 'cyclops' before 'welded' before 'outcast', because outcast vocabulary (rust, salvage, weathering) is generic enough to steal a record that is really a cyclops shot in a corroded environment.

outcast.label: Outcast (ferro pole)
outcast.description: Field-repaired androids degraded by the planet. The good guys. Asymmetric by repair history, accidental seams, warm sodium light, zero body neon, reads as individual.

cyclops.label: Cyclops (chrome pole)
cyclops.description: Factory-new single-optic antagonists. Perfectly symmetric, designed shutlines, unmarked chrome and carbon fibre, cold body neon, identical units. Reads as product.

welded.label: Welded (cyborg)
welded.description: Human flesh and machine, neither fully. The only register permitted bare skin. Partial, intermittent, or failing neon. Mixed seam grammar.

contact.label: Contact (two registers, one frame)
contact.description: Outcast and cyclops (or welded) sharing one frame under one light. Proves the registers obey a single rendering law.

material.label: Material macro
material.description: Close studies teaching the physics directly — weave scale, chrome curvature, emitter falloff.

training_profiles.intended_use: The ferrochrome house style LoRA — one style, three registers. Registers are carried by caption vocabulary and prompt, NOT by separate adapters.
training_profiles._eligible_lanes_note: Deliberately EMPTY. The lane-mismatch gotcha drops every row when this is populated (same trap documented on rustline-style-lora). All five lanes feed one style LoRA by design — see lanes.json _law.
